speaker: Ms Anthea Ong
text: asked the Minister for Law (a) whether an extension of the Protection from Harassment Act to cover entities will impose vicarious liability onto employers; and (b) if not, whether the Government plans to move away from the present individual criminal liability-based approach.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Law)
text: Apart from POHA, there are many pieces of legislation that cover both entities and individuals.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Law)
text: Likewise, in the Protection from Online Falsehoods and Manipulation Act (POFMA), the word "person" refers to individuals in Part 3 and to entities, such as Internet platforms and mass media service providers, in Part 4.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Law)
text: The law, meaning Common Law, provides for various ways of attributing vicarious liability.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Law)
text: Likewise, there are principles laid down in case law establishing when an individual can be held criminally liable for the acts of an entity.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Law)
text: POFMA empowers a Minister to issue Directions to an Internet intermediary.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Law)
text: If an intermediary fails to comply with a Direction without reasonable excuse, its executives may be held liable for that non-compliance if, for example, they are found to have abetted the non-compliance.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Law)
text: They may be found to have abetted the non-compliance if they had, amongst other things, suggested, supported or encouraged the non-compliance, whether by words or by their silence.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Law)
text: The Member's second question is whether the Government plans to move away from the present "individual criminal liability-based approach".

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Law)
text: Criminal liability can be imposed on both entities and individuals when they commit criminal offences.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Law)
text: That is already the position in law today.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: Could I please follow up with two supplementary questions?

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: The first is, I understand that in POHA, as much as entities are included, they are included insofar as they can seek protection from harassment, but they are not actually liable if they are the ones harassing.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: So, can the Senior Parliamentary Secretary clarify that because that is the understanding that we have of POHA?

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: In relation to the question being specific to the employer, the concern here is about workplace harassment.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: So, whether the employer has the liability in addition to responsibility in maintaining a workplace that is free from harassment and violence.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: I would also like to understand what was the intention behind us extending POHA to include entities in terms of being protected but not in terms of them being liable as the harassing party.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: I think the third and first questions are in a way related, so I will try and handle them together.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: But I would like to add that in section 3 of POHA, an individual or entity must not, with intent, cause harassment, alarm or distress to another person by a series of means.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: It is actually already expressly provided for in the provisions themselves.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: So, that is section 3, subsection (1), for harassment under POHA.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: So, there are sections in POHA which make it quite clear that entities can be criminally liable.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: So, that is one set of the Member's questions.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Any proposed changes must be thoroughly thought out.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: This was a point that was also made by the Penal Code Review Committee in its report.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Yesterday, I heard the exchange that the Member had with Minister for Manpower Josephine Teo.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: It was in relation to Singapore's abstention from the vote on the International Labour Organization's Convention on Workplace Violence and Harassment.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: So, that is another means, apart from criminal law, whereby employees can seek comfort in.
